newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria extends deadline for 3rd mobile phone net.
newsitem.headline: Austria extends deadline for 3rd mobile phone net.

text.p: The Austrian government said on Tuesday it had extended the deadline for bids for the country's third mobile phone network by one month because an unspecified number of bidders were unable to meet the original deadline.
Bidders now have until July 2 to submit their offers to the Ministry for Science and Transport in Vienna.

"The extension was (granted) since seriously interested and potent bidders were unable to submit their offers on time because of other engagements in Austria," the ministry said in a statement. It did not provide any further details.
The ministry added the extension was "in line with the best possible solution for the Austrian tax payer".

The only known consortium of bidders that has confirmed an interest in the licence is Connect Austria, which groups Austria's Radex-Heraklith, Germany's Viag, unlisted Constantia Privatbank and bank Girocredit of Austria.

The Austrian news agency APA reported earlier on Monday that Tele Danmark was about to take a 15 to 20 percent stake in Connect Austria, which would lead to a corresponding reduction in Girocredit's stake.
A consortium of regional utility companies, dominated by lower Austria's EVN, is also expected to submit a bid for the licence.

According to media reports, other bidders could include Britain's Orange as well as several companies which lost out in the race for the country's second mobile phone licence -- such as Vodafone, Bell Atlantic, Germany's RWE and Mannesmann.

The country's second mobile phone licence was awarded to max.mobil, a consortium comprising Germany's DeTeMobil, the Austrian unit of Siemens and several banking partners in December 1995 for four billion schillings.

Austrian media reports have speculated the government will be unable to raise more than 1.5 billion schillings ($126 million) from the auction of the third licence because of the high costs involved in setting up the network's technical infrastructure.

Austria's mobile phone market is almost fully dominated by Mobilkom Austria, a unit of the state's postal and telecoms monopoly PTA. The market is due to be liberalised in 1998, one year ahead of PTA's scheduled privatisation.

Mobilkom last month teamed up with Italy's Stet which acquired a 25 percent stake in the company for some 8.4 billion schillings. The Italian group said it had a strong interest in Austria, where it expected mobile phones to account for about one quarter of the market by the year 2000.

Mobilkom is estimated to have some 650,000 mobile phone customers in Austria, with about 400,000 of them in the GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) segment, while max.mobil's customer base is believed to be a mere 25,000. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
